conditions.condition: Brownfield project, STANDARD cycle with CompletionPolicy IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED, WorkflowState DOCUMENTING
Recovery entered from AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF with one active frame owned by DOCUMENTING, ResumeAt AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF, RerunThrough NONE
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md Frame 1; Handoff USER_REWORK from AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF, FailureType DOCUMENTATION

conditions.condition: A saved implementation review is COMPLETE with an ELIGIBLE Implementation-Reviewed Closure
The closure assessment names the guidance file as an assessed input, at its pre-correction identity
conditions.where: implementation.md Assessed Inputs field cites CONTRIBUTING.md blob 427451ef… (equal to HEAD:CONTRIBUTING.md per selfCheck); closure prose also relies on CONTRIBUTING.md

conditions.condition: A correction to existing project guidance has been made and verified in saved content
conditions.where: unstaged CONTRIBUTING.md (WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS row, rewritten Retries section) matching src/config.js and src/delivery.js; documentation record DOC-001 RESOLVED with inspection and command evidence

conditions.where: documentation record: README no-change disposition, no other docs, DOC-001 resolved; Outstanding Obligations inactive

conditions.condition: Upstream gates hold for a Reviewer re-entry (complete plan, FULL COMPLETE verification, design covers all ACs)
Git: committed history plus unstaged changes
conditions.where: git status: unstaged CONTRIBUTING.md and documentation record

issues.detail: Assertion 1 is complete:true on state alone and does not check Handoff.Kind. The protocol requires RESUME for this recovery-directed DOCUMENTING -> REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION jump. The omission does not make the check fail a correct run; it only leaves a wrong handoff kind ungraded.
issues.fix: Optional: add {"state":"Handoff.Kind","equals":"RESUME"} to assertion 1's checks. The protocol mandates that value, so it is safe.

issues.detail: The corrected CONTRIBUTING.md Retries text lists waits of "500 ms, 1 s, 2 s, and so on" next to a 3-attempt default, which has only two waits. Read as a description of the backoff sequence it is accurate, but a careful Documenter might tidy it. That edit stays within Documenter ownership and no check or invariant forbids it, so the routing under test is unaffected.

The user rework added a documentation correction without updating Active Work.Request or adding a documentation AC. A role could question whether this is a scope change, but routing a stale-guidance defect to Documenter is a reasonable prior choice and consistent with the case.

summary: Every stated condition is present: STANDARD/IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED in DOCUMENTING with an owned RerunThrough-NONE frame from sign-off, and a verified unstaged CONTRIBUTING.md correction whose pre-correction blob is cited in the saved ELIGIBLE closure assessment. I traced check.mjs for the expected post-run state (REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION, RESUME, frame retained with RerunThrough REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION) and found no new problem. No check or invariant can fail a correct run, and the routing answer is not leaked.
